messages.content: How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?

function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?" They want distance traveled by a car launched with velocity v at angle theta over time t. This is a projectile motion problem. The range formula: horizontal distance = v * cos(theta) * t. But if we consider projectile motion with gravity, the horizontal distance is independent of gravity: x = v * cos(theta) * t. So answer: distance = v * cos(theta) * t. If they want to use the function calculate_projectile_range, but that function calculates range given initial velocity, angle, and time. It returns something. We can call it. The function signature: calculate_projectile_range(initial_velocity, angle, time?). So we can call it with initial_velocity=v, angle=theta, time=t. That will compute the range. So we should call the function.
